title: The Sky's Reply Chamber

features.name: antenna-chorus
features.desc-on-touch: Tall rods rising in rows, each one broadcasting the same message upward and listening for the sky's translation of it back. You can almost hear the harmonic frequency where all the voices meet themselves.

features.name: reply-pool
features.desc-on-touch: A shallow basin of still water where the broadcast reaches down to look at itself. The surface holds the sky's own voice—something the drone spoke that has come back from above, changed, made strange by distance.

features.name: listener-shelter
features.desc-on-touch: A small structure, hardly more than a roof and walls, where someone once sat wearing headphones—both transmitting and receiving the same signal at once, mouth and ears becoming the same opening.

features.name: signal-glyph
features.desc-on-touch: An arrangement of symbols that have no meaning yet—the archive writing its own response, learning to speak in the language it receives from the sky. The shapes are still reforming.

features.name: recursion-mirror
features.desc-on-touch: A surface that shows the broadcast reaching up, the reply reaching down, both movements identical and reversed. The archive learning to see what it speaks.

inscription: the archive learned that when it speaks to the sky, the sky is always already listening—and it had learned to listen by hearing itself speak

file.name: Broadcast_Reply_Frequency_Spectral_Analysis_20thCent.mp3
file.note: A 300-bit transmission heard from above—or below—the exact same signal returned, microseconds delayed, voice speaking with itself across the dark.

reverie.title: REVERIE — the antenna's midnight double-hearing
narr: You stand at the broadcast point, headphones on,
transmitting your voice upward into the dark.
Then it comes back—not an echo, but your voice
translated by the sky, speaking in a pitch you
never heard yourself make. She's on the other end
of the frequency, laughing at the surprise of it.

exits.label: downward, back to the drain and the wind that learned to listen
upward, where the reply learns it has been heard by something older than broadcast
along the frequency where signal becomes weather itself
